name: PCOS-friendly South Asian
summary: PCOS-friendly home cooking from Punjab, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Pakistan: dal, chana and vegetables, millet, jowar and brown basmati as the slower-digesting starch, protein at every meal and fatty fish three times.
howItWorks:
**Protein and fibre at every meal.** Breakfast is moong chilla, egg bhurji or a millet pongal, so you start the day with protein. Dal, rajma, chickpeas and sprouts make the base of lunch and dinner, with chicken, fish, paneer and yogurt alongside.

**Slower starch.** Each meal has one portion of a slower-digesting grain: a roti, jowar, foxtail millet or brown basmati. Vegetables, raita and kachumber fill the rest of the plate.

**Regular meals, three fish dinners.** Three meals and one or two snacks a day, so nobody goes long without eating. Salmon on Tuesday, mackerel on Friday and trout on Sunday bring omega-3 fats, always cooked fresh.

**Cook once, eat twice.** The chicken tikka, keema, sambar and Saturday's biryani each make two portions, so the next day's lunch is already done. Rotis are best cooked fresh, but a spare one warms up fine in a dry pan. Wash produce before you cut it, and wash the board and your hands after raw chicken or fish.

**Lighter days.** On the Light size the second snack drops away and the cooking uses a little less oil, ghee, paneer and toor dal. The grain stays much the same: a small, palm-sized roti or about half a cup of cooked rice or millet.

recipes.name: Moong chilla with paneer and spinach, mint yogurt dip
recipes.about: Thin, golden pancakes of ground yellow moong dal with onion, grated carrot and spinach, folded around a little crumbled paneer and served with a cool mint yogurt dip. Moong dal and paneer together make this a breakfast with **plenty of protein and fibre**.

ingredients.note: split yellow moong dal, soaked for 4 hours or overnight
half in the batter, half in the dip
half in the batter, half in the paneer

steps: Drain the soaked dal and blend it with the ginger, half the green chili, the hing, the turmeric, the salt and a few spoonfuls of cold water until smooth. The batter should pour like thin pancake batter.
Stir the spinach, carrot, onion, cumin and half the cilantro into the batter.
Mash the paneer with the chaat masala and the rest of the cilantro. For the dip, blitz or stir the yogurt with the mint, the rest of the green chili and a pinch of salt.

Warm a non-stick pan over medium heat and wipe it with a little of the oil. Pour in a ladle of batter and spread it into a thin round. Cook until the top looks set and the underside is golden with brown spots, about 3 minutes.
Drizzle a few drops of oil around the edge, flip and cook for 1 minute more. Spoon some paneer down the middle and fold. Repeat with the rest and serve hot with the dip.
recipes.inspiredBy: Punjabi and Gujarati moong dal cheela, filled the way a street stall folds it
recipes.tip: Soak the dal the night before and mornings take about 25 minutes. If a chilla tears, the pan is too cool or the batter too thick.

recipes.name: Masala egg bhurji with a small whole-wheat roti
recipes.about: Soft, well-set scrambled eggs with onion, tomato, green peas, spinach and ginger, scooped up with a small whole-wheat roti and a bowl of cold yogurt. The eggs and yogurt bring **protein to start the day**, and the roti adds whole grain.
steps: Mix the atta with a pinch of salt and enough warm water to make a soft dough. Cover it and rest while you make the bhurji.
Warm the oil in a pan, add the cumin and let it sizzle, then the onion, ginger and green chili. Cook until the onion is soft and golden, about 6 minutes.
Add the tomato, peas, spinach, turmeric and Kashmiri chili. Cook until the tomato breaks down, the spinach wilts and the peas are tender, about 5 minutes.
Pour in the eggs and the salt. Stir gently over medium-low heat until the eggs are completely set with no runny egg left, about 3 minutes. Stir in the cilantro.
Roll the dough into a thin round and cook it on a hot dry pan, turning once, until it has brown spots and puffs a little. Serve with the bhurji and the yogurt.
recipes.inspiredBy: Pakistani and Punjabi anda bhurji with peas
recipes.tip: Roll and cook two or three extra rotis on Sunday evening and they reheat fine in a dry pan.

recipes.name: Foxtail millet and moong pongal with curd
recipes.about: A soft, peppery pongal of foxtail millet and split moong dal, tempered with ghee, black pepper, cumin and curry leaves, with carrot and green peas stirred through. A bowl of curd on the side adds **protein and calcium**.

ingredients.note: plain, with a pinch of cumin

steps: Rinse the millet and dal together. Put them in a pot with the carrot, peas, ginger, the salt and about four times their volume of water.

Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low heat, stirring now and then, until the millet and dal are very soft and a little porridge-like, about 25 minutes. Add a splash of hot water if it gets too thick.
In a small pan, warm the ghee. Add the cumin, the black pepper, the curry leaves and the hing. Sizzle for about 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Pour the tempering over the pongal and stir well. Serve hot with the yogurt.
recipes.inspiredBy: Tamil ven pongal, made with thinai (foxtail millet) in place of rice
recipes.tip: Make a double pot the evening before, chill it within 1 hour, and reheat it with a splash of water to 74 C (165 F) once.

recipes.name: Punjabi rajma masala with brown basmati and cucumber raita
recipes.about: Kidney beans simmered in a thick onion-tomato masala, with a small mound of brown basmati and a cool cucumber raita on the side. The beans and yogurt together carry **protein and fibre**, and the rice soaks up the gravy.
steps: Drain the soaked rajma, cover with fresh water and boil hard for 10 minutes, then simmer until the beans are completely soft and mash easily between your fingers, about 45 minutes (20 minutes in a pressure cooker).
Meanwhile, cook the brown basmati in plenty of boiling water until tender, about 25 minutes, then drain.
Warm the oil in a pan, add the cumin and bay leaf, then the onion. Cook until deep golden, about 8 minutes. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomato, Kashmiri chili, ground coriander and salt. Cook until the tomato collapses and the oil separates, about 6 minutes.
Add the beans with their cooking water. Simmer for 15 minutes, mashing a few beans against the side to thicken the gravy. Stir in the garam masala and half the cilantro.
Stir the grated cucumber and the rest of the cilantro into the yogurt with a pinch of salt. Serve the rajma over the rice with the raita on the side.
recipes.inspiredBy: Punjabi rajma chawal, with brown basmati and a big bowl of raita
recipes.tip: Cook the beans in a pressure cooker and the whole dish takes about 40 minutes. Squeeze the grated cucumber first so the raita stays thick.

recipes.name: Tandoori chicken tikka with missi roti and kachumber
recipes.about: Chunks of chicken marinated in yogurt, ginger, garlic and Kashmiri chili, baked until charred at the edges, with a crunchy carrot kachumber and a small missi roti made with chickpea flour. Dinner is **high in protein**, and the second portion becomes tomorrow's lunch.

ingredients.note: half for the marinade, half for the mint raita

steps: Mix half the yogurt with most of the lemon juice, grated ginger and garlic, Kashmiri chili, garam masala and half the salt. Spoon a little of the marinade into a small bowl for the cauliflower, then coat the chicken in the rest. Never reuse marinade that touched raw chicken. Cover and marinate the chicken in the fridge for at least 1 hour, or overnight, and wash the board and your hands after.

Heat the oven to 230 C (450 F). Spread the chicken and the cauliflower florets (tossed with the marinade you set aside) on a rack set over a tray and roast for 20 to 25 minutes, turning once, until the edges are charred and there is no pink inside. Check the thickest piece with a thermometer: it should read 74 C (165 F).

For the missi roti, mix the atta, the besan, the ajwain (rubbed between your palms) and a pinch of salt with a little oil and warm water into a soft dough. Rest for 10 minutes, then roll into thin rounds and cook on a hot dry pan until brown-spotted.

Make the kachumber: toss the tomato, grated carrot and onion with the chaat masala and the rest of the lemon juice. Stir the chopped mint and a pinch of salt into the rest of the yogurt for the raita.

Serve half the chicken with a roti, the kachumber and the raita. Spread the second portion in a shallow dish, cool it, refrigerate it within 1 hour and pack it for tomorrow's lunch. Reheat once, until it reaches 74 C (165 F) all the way through.
recipes.inspiredBy: Punjabi chicken tikka, baked in the oven, with besan and whole-wheat missi roti
recipes.tip: Roll and cook all the rotis fresh; they are best warm. The leftover chicken is lovely in a dry pan with a squeeze of lemon.

recipes.name: Masoor dal with spinach, a small roti and cucumber raita
recipes.about: Quick-cooking pink lentils simmered with a big pile of spinach and finished with a sizzling garlic and cumin tadka. A small whole-wheat roti and a cool cucumber raita turn it into a lunch with **protein and iron**.
steps: Put the lentils in a pot with the turmeric, tomato and about four times their volume of water. Bring to a boil and skim off any foam. Simmer until completely soft, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the spinach and a pinch of salt and cook for 3 minutes more until wilted. Mash the dal lightly with a spoon.
Warm the oil and ghee in a small pan. Add the cumin, then the onion, garlic and ginger. Cook until the onion is golden, about 6 minutes. Add the Kashmiri chili and pour the tadka over the dal.
Mix the atta with a pinch of salt and warm water into a soft dough, rest it for 10 minutes, then roll thin and cook on a hot dry pan until brown-spotted.
Stir the cucumber and a pinch of salt into the yogurt. Serve the dal with the roti and the raita.
recipes.inspiredBy: Punjabi dal palak with pink lentils
recipes.tip: Frozen spinach works: use it straight from the freezer and cook a minute longer.

recipes.name: Tandoori-style salmon with roasted cauliflower and carrot and chickpea kachumber
recipes.about: Salmon fillet marinated in yogurt, lemon and Kashmiri chili, baked until it flakes, with roasted cauliflower, carrots and a chickpea kachumber. The salmon brings **omega-3 fats and vitamin D**, and the chickpeas, carrot and cauliflower carry the fibre.

ingredients.note: skin-on fillet, cut into two pieces
half for the marinade, half for the mint drizzle

steps: Mix half the yogurt with half the lemon juice, grated ginger and garlic, Kashmiri chili, ajwain and half the salt. Coat the salmon, cover and marinate in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 220 C (425 F). Toss the cauliflower and carrot with the oil, ground cumin and a pinch of salt on a tray and roast for 10 minutes.

Add the salmon to the tray, skin side down, and roast for another 10 to 12 minutes, until the fish flakes easily with a fork (70 C / 158 F in the thickest part) and the cauliflower is browned at the edges.
Toss the chickpeas, cucumber, tomato, onion and the chaat masala with the rest of the lemon juice for the kachumber.
Stir the chopped mint into the rest of the yogurt with a pinch of salt. Serve the salmon on the kachumber with the roasted vegetables and a spoon of mint yogurt.
recipes.inspiredBy: Punjabi and Pakistani tandoori machli, baked in the oven
recipes.tip: Skin-on salmon holds together best. Eat this fresh rather than as a leftover.

recipes.name: Chicken keema matar with jowar roti
recipes.about: Minced chicken thigh cooked down with onion, tomato, ginger, finely chopped cauliflower and sweet green peas, with a handful of cilantro to finish and a jowar (sorghum) roti. It is **rich in protein**, the peas add fibre, and the second portion is ready for tomorrow's lunch.

ingredients.note: skinless, minced by the butcher or pulsed in a food processor
half finely chopped for the keema, half thinly sliced for the side
whisked, stirred in off the heat

steps: Warm the oil in a wide pan, add the cumin, then the chopped onion. Cook until deep golden, about 8 minutes. Add the ginger and garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomato, turmeric, Kashmiri chili, ground coriander and salt. Cook until the tomato collapses and the oil separates, about 6 minutes.

Add the minced chicken and break it up with a spoon. Cook, stirring, until it is no longer pink, then add the peas, the cauliflower and a splash of water. Cover and simmer for 12 minutes until a thermometer in the meat reads 74 C (165 F) and the peas are tender.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the whisked yogurt and the garam masala, and finish with the cilantro.

For the roti, knead the jowar flour with a pinch of salt and hot water into a soft dough while it is warm. Divide it into two balls, one for each portion, and pat them out on a damp cloth or between two sheets of parchment, then lift onto a hot dry pan and cook until brown-spotted. Jowar is delicate, so be gentle.

Toss the sliced onion with the lemon juice and the chaat masala for a quick laccha pyaaz, and serve half the keema with the roti and the onion. Spread the second portion in a shallow dish, cool it, refrigerate it within 1 hour and reheat once tomorrow, until it reaches 74 C (165 F) all the way through. Wrap the second roti in a clean cloth and pack it with the keema.
recipes.inspiredBy: Punjabi and Pakistani keema matar, with minced chicken and a Gujarati-style jowar roti
recipes.tip: No jowar flour? Use whole-wheat atta. Keema freezes well for up to 3 months: thaw it in the fridge, eat it within 2 days and reheat it once until it reaches 74 C (165 F) all the way through.

recipes.name: Vegetable sambar with foxtail millet and curd
recipes.about: A tangy toor dal sambar with drumstick, brinjal and carrot, spooned over foxtail millet with a bowl of curd on the side. The dal and curd give it **protein and fibre**, and the second portion is lunch tomorrow.

ingredients.note: plain, as curd on the side

steps: Cook the toor dal with the turmeric and about four times its volume of water until completely soft, about 25 minutes (10 minutes in a pressure cooker). Mash lightly.
In another pot, simmer the drumstick, brinjal, carrot, onion and tomato in a little water with the tamarind paste, sambar powder and salt until the vegetables are just tender, about 12 minutes.
Stir the dal into the vegetables and simmer for 8 minutes. Add water if it is too thick, as sambar should be pourable.
Cook the millet in two and a half times its volume of water until fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Warm the oil in a small pan. Add the mustard seeds, and when they pop, the curry leaves and hing. Pour the tempering into the sambar.

Serve the sambar over the millet with the curd on the side. Cool the second portion in a shallow dish, refrigerate it within 1 hour and reheat once tomorrow, until it reaches 74 C (165 F) all the way through.
recipes.inspiredBy: Tamil Nadu sambar with drumstick and brinjal, served over millet
recipes.tip: Drumstick pods are chewed and the tough fibre left on the plate. Frozen drumstick works well.

recipes.name: Pepper mackerel fry with cabbage poriyal and millet
recipes.about: Atlantic mackerel fillet rubbed with crushed black pepper, ginger and curry leaves and pan-fried until crisp, with a quick cabbage poriyal tempered with chana dal and fresh coconut. The mackerel is rich in **omega-3 fats and vitamin D**.
steps: Mix the crushed pepper, grated ginger and garlic, half the lemon juice, turmeric, Kashmiri chili and half the salt into a paste. Rub it over the mackerel and rest for 15 minutes.
Cook the millet in two and a half times its volume of water until fluffy, about 15 minutes.

Warm half the oil in a non-stick pan. Fry the mackerel with half the curry leaves for about 4 minutes on each side, until crisp and golden and the fish flakes easily (70 C / 158 F in the thickest part).
For the poriyal, warm the rest of the oil. Add the mustard seeds, and when they pop, the chana dal and the rest of the curry leaves. Cook until the dal is golden, about 1 minute.
Add the onion and cook until soft, then the cabbage, the rest of the salt and a splash of water. Cover and cook until just tender, about 5 minutes. Stir in the coconut.
Serve the fish with the poriyal and the millet, with the rest of the lemon squeezed over.
recipes.inspiredBy: Tamil Nadu milagu meen varuval, with a Tamil-style cabbage poriyal
recipes.tip: Make the poriyal while the fish rests. Use Atlantic mackerel, or Indian mackerel (ayala or bangda), not kingfish, surmai or vanjaram, which are higher in mercury. Thaw frozen fillets in the fridge and cook them within 2 days. Cook the fish fresh and do not keep it as a leftover.

recipes.name: Gujarati-style sprouted moong usal with jowar roti and curd
recipes.about: Whole green moong, sprouted for a day and then simmered with onion, tomato and a little coconut, with a small jowar roti and a bowl of curd. Sprouted moong cooks quickly and gives **protein and plenty of fibre**.

ingredients.note: whole green moong, soaked overnight and sprouted for a day
plain, as curd on the side

steps: Rinse the sprouted moong. Sprouted beans must be cooked thoroughly, so boil them in plenty of water at a rolling boil for 15 to 20 minutes, until completely soft. Drain, keeping a little of the water.
Warm the oil in a pan. Add the mustard seeds and cumin, and when the mustard pops, add the onion, ginger and garlic. Cook until golden, about 7 minutes.

Add the tomato, turmeric, Kashmiri chili and salt and cook until soft, about 5 minutes. Add the moong with a few spoonfuls of the cooking water, the garam masala, the peanuts and the coconut. Simmer for 8 minutes.

Knead the jowar flour with a pinch of salt and hot water into a soft dough while it is warm. Shape it into one ball and pat it into a small round on a damp cloth or between two sheets of parchment, then lift it onto a hot dry pan and cook until brown-spotted on both sides.
Serve the usal with the roti, the sliced cucumber and the curd, scattered with cilantro.
recipes.inspiredBy: Gujarati and Maharashtrian usal, with whole moong cooked until completely soft
recipes.tip: Soak the moong the night before, drain it in a colander, cover with a damp cloth and it sprouts in about a day. Rinse twice. Store-bought moong sprouts also work; the 15 to 20 minute boil in step 1 covers both.

recipes.name: Chicken dum biryani with brown basmati and cucumber salad
recipes.about: A weekend biryani: chicken marinated in yogurt and spices, layered with brown basmati, cauliflower, peas, mint and golden onions and toasted almonds and steamed on the dum. It is a project, but one pot makes two big portions, so Sunday lunch is done. The rice shares the pot with **lots of chicken and vegetables**.
steps: Marinate the chicken in the yogurt with the grated ginger and garlic, Kashmiri chili, turmeric, garam masala, half the mint and cilantro and half the salt. Chill for at least 1 hour.

Fry the sliced onion in the oil over medium heat, stirring often, until deep golden, about 15 minutes. Add the almonds for the last 2 minutes. Set half the onion and all the almonds aside for the top.
Soak the rice for 30 minutes, then boil it in plenty of water with the bay leaf, cardamom, cinnamon, clove and the rest of the salt until about 80% cooked, about 20 minutes. Drain.
In a heavy pot, cook the marinated chicken with the rest of the onions for 10 minutes. Add the cauliflower and peas.

Spread the half-cooked rice over the chicken. Top with the reserved onion and almonds, most of the rest of the mint and cilantro, the ghee and 3 tablespoons of water. Seal the pot with foil and a tight lid and steam on the lowest heat for 25 minutes.

Rest for 10 minutes. Make sure the chicken reads 74 C (165 F) in the thickest piece and the rice is tender. Toss the cucumber with the last of the mint and a pinch of salt for the salad. Serve half. Spread the second portion in a shallow dish, cool it, refrigerate it within 1 hour and eat it the next day, reheated once until it reaches 74 C (165 F) all the way through.
recipes.inspiredBy: Hyderabadi and Pakistani chicken dum biryani, packed with vegetables and made with brown basmati
recipes.tip: Brown basmati is chewier than white, so give it the full 80% cook before layering. Cook the rice that morning, cool it in a shallow tray and chill it within 1 hour, and the layering takes 20 minutes.

recipes.name: Lahori-style trout tawa fry with chickpea and spinach
recipes.about: Rainbow trout fillet coated in a spiced chickpea-flour crust and pan-fried until crisp, with a quick sauté of chickpeas and spinach and a small whole-wheat roti. The trout brings **omega-3 fats and vitamin D**, and the chickpeas and spinach add fibre and iron.
steps: Mix the chickpea flour, ajwain, Kashmiri chili, half the lemon juice, the grated ginger and garlic and half the salt with a spoonful of water into a thick paste. Smear it over the trout and rest for 15 minutes.
Mix the atta with a pinch of salt and warm water into a soft dough and rest it while you cook.

For the chana palak, warm a little of the oil in a pan. Add the cumin and the onion and cook until golden. Add the tomato and cook until soft, about 4 minutes, then the chickpeas and spinach. Cook until the spinach wilts, about 4 minutes, and finish with a pinch of salt and a squeeze of lemon.

Heat the rest of the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Fry the trout for about 4 minutes on each side, until the coating is crisp and the fish flakes easily with a fork (70 C / 158 F in the thickest part).
Roll and cook the roti on a hot dry pan until brown-spotted. Serve the fish with the chana palak, the roti and lemon wedges, dusted with chaat masala.
recipes.inspiredBy: Lahori fried fish (machli), pan-fried in a little oil with ajwain, and a quick chana palak
recipes.tip: Do not move the fish while the coating sets, or it will tear. Cook fresh and eat the same day.

recipes.name: Salted jeera chaas
recipes.about: A thin, cooling glass of yogurt whisked with water, roasted cumin and mint, the kind you would drink after a heavy meal. It is a **high-protein sip** with no added sugar.

ingredients.note: roasted in a dry pan and ground

steps: Toast the cumin in a dry pan for 30 seconds until fragrant, then grind it.
Whisk the yogurt with about a cup of cold water until smooth and pourable.
Stir in the cumin, the black salt, the salt and the chopped mint. Serve over ice or very cold.
recipes.inspiredBy: Punjabi and Pakistani salted chaas, with roasted cumin

recipes.name: Mint and cucumber chaas
recipes.about: Yogurt blended with cucumber, mint and a pinch of cumin into a green, refreshing drink. It is a light way to add **protein and calcium** between meals.
steps: Roughly chop the cucumber and put it in a blender with the yogurt, mint, cumin, lemon juice, salt and about half a cup of cold water.
Blend until smooth and pour into a glass. Serve cold.
recipes.inspiredBy: Gujarati and Pakistani cucumber chaas

recipes.name: Masala almonds with cucumber
recipes.about: A small handful of almonds tossed with chaat masala, a pinch of chili and lemon, toasted until fragrant, with cool cucumber sticks. Almonds are a good source of **vitamin E and healthy fats**.
steps: Toast the almonds in a dry pan over medium heat, shaking often, until fragrant and lightly browned, about 4 minutes.
Toss them with the chaat masala, Kashmiri chili, salt and lemon while warm.
Serve with the cucumber sticks.
recipes.inspiredBy: Pakistani and Punjabi spiced nuts, pan-toasted with chaat masala
recipes.tip: Toast a jar of almonds on Sunday and add the spices on the day.

recipes.name: Guava and apple chaat with yogurt
recipes.about: Diced guava and apple tossed with chaat masala and a lemony yogurt, with slivered almonds for crunch. Guava is a good source of **vitamin C and fibre**, and the yogurt means the fruit does not come alone.

ingredients.note: diced, ripe but firm, or thawed frozen cubes from an Indian grocer

steps: Wash the fruit well and dice it with the skin on.
Stir the lemon juice and chaat masala into the yogurt.
Toss the fruit with the yogurt and scatter over the almonds.
recipes.inspiredBy: Pakistani fruit chaat, with yogurt and almonds
recipes.tip: No guava? A ripe pear works.

recipes.name: Masala roasted chickpeas
recipes.about: No-salt-added chickpeas roasted until crisp and tossed with chaat masala and lemon. A handful has **fibre and plant protein** and keeps you going until dinner.

ingredients.note: no-salt-added, drained, rinsed and patted very dry

steps: Heat the oven to 210 C (400 F). Toss the dry chickpeas with the oil on a tray.
Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, shaking the tray halfway, until crisp and golden.
Toss with the chaat masala, Kashmiri chili, salt and lemon while hot. They crisp up as they cool.
recipes.inspiredBy: Punjabi and Pakistani chana, oven-crisped with chaat masala
recipes.tip: Roast a double batch; they stay crisp in a jar for 3 days.

recipes.name: Masala egg chaat with tomato and onion
recipes.about: A hard-boiled egg, chopped and tossed with tomato, onion, chaat masala, black pepper and lemon, the way a street cart in Lahore or Karachi makes anda chaat. An egg gives a quick hit of **protein and choline**.

ingredients.note: boiled until the yolk is firm

steps: Lower the egg into boiling water and simmer for 10 minutes, so the yolk is fully set. Cool it in cold water and peel.
Chop the egg and toss it with the tomato, onion, chaat masala, pepper and lemon.
Eat straight away, or chill and eat the same day.
recipes.inspiredBy: Pakistani street-style anda chaat

recipes.name: Warm moong sprout chaat
recipes.about: Moong sprouts boiled until tender and tossed with tomato, onion, lemon, chaat masala and a few roasted peanuts. A bowl brings **fibre and plant protein** with a pleasing crunch.
steps: Bring a small pot of water to a boil, add the sprouts and boil for 5 minutes at a rolling boil until completely soft. Raw sprouts can carry bacteria, so do not skip this. Drain well and eat the same day.
Toss the warm sprouts with the tomato, onion, lemon juice, chaat masala and cilantro.
Top with the peanuts and eat warm.
recipes.inspiredBy: Pakistani and Gujarati sprout chaat, with the sprouts boiled until soft

recipes.name: Apple chaat with yogurt and peanuts
recipes.about: Crisp diced apple with yogurt, chaat masala, a squeeze of lemon and a spoonful of roasted peanuts. The peanuts add crunch and **protein**, and the yogurt keeps the fruit from standing alone.
steps: Wash the apple well and dice it with the skin on. Toss it with the lemon juice so it stays bright.
Stir the chaat masala into the yogurt.
Fold the apple into the yogurt and scatter over the peanuts.
recipes.inspiredBy: Pakistani fruit chaat, with crisp apple and yogurt
